my_lead: 5r (co-named with 5p in the abstract as best antibacterial/antioxidant; 5r is also one of the two docked compounds, called 'most potent')

reactions.issue: 4-fluoro-3-nitrobenzoic acid + MeOH/H2SO4 (MW 80 C 10 min, 95%) -> methyl ester 2. Methanol supplies the OMe so listing it is justified (it is also the solvent).

SNAr of 2 with 4-fluoroaniline (written '4-fluorophenyl aniline' in the text) in DMF, MW 80 C 5 min, 90% -> 3. The volume/mmol given (0.36 mL, 2.34 mmol) does not quite fit 4-fluoroaniline's density, but the product name fixes the reagent.
Zn/ammonium formate/MeOH rt 10 min, 92% -> amine 4 (reductant supplies no atoms, correctly not listed).
4 + 2,3,4-trihydroxybenzaldehyde 1:1 neat MW 110 C 8 min (Table 1), 85% -> 5r. Regiochemistry checked: ester para to the N-aryl carbon = 1-aryl-5-carboxylate; matches SMILES.

leaf_issues: 2,3,4-trihydroxybenzaldehyde and 4-fluoroaniline are not named in the text (Table 1 gives '2,3,4-(OH)3 Ph'); deduced from names. Support for all leaves: 'All chemicals were supplied by Sigma-Aldrich via Capital Lab, South Africa.' (general sentence only).
notes: 4 steps from commercial materials. Lead is co-named (5p/5r, and 5e for antifungal); 5r is an acceptable choice; 5p would use the same route with 2-hydroxy-4,6-dimethoxybenzaldehyde. The JSON's 'fluoroaniline' product names for 3 and 4 are the paper's own odd nomenclature.
